analysis:
Examined the Autopilot changes: AutopilotStartInventory.swift (new), ModelAutopilotPolicy.swift, ModelAutopilotSettings.swift (comment only), ProviderLoop+Autopilot.swift, ProviderLoop+AutopilotBusy.swift (new) and the file_changes excerpt of ProviderLoop+AutopilotControl.swift.

No concrete regression found. Observations:
- ModelAutopilotPolicy.swift:21-23 adds bounds on holdSeconds (0...86400) and rejects a hold without a load target. This is fail-closed and consistent with the existing lease bound.
- ProviderLoop+Autopilot.swift:56-62 attaches the new report fields (capabilities, adopted/held models, busy reasons, stalls, download storage) only when autopilotConsented. Line 279 sends `detail` only when consented. Without consent the snapshot stays at protocol 3. The busy-reason refactor in ProviderLoop+AutopilotBusy.swift is meant to be equivalent to the old inline busy expression. All 20 old conditions appear present and `.autopilotOperation` is excluded from the policy input, so the load-admission gate is not weakened. Cancellation rechecks (lines 215-226) are fail-closed.
- AutopilotStartInventory.swift:38-88 widens the Autopilot set from the persisted selection to cached builds whose weight hash matches the coordinator catalog. When the catalog is unreachable it falls back to a local download ledger plus a hash match. The ledger is operator-writable, but the operator can already swap weights (T-012), so this adds no new capability beyond the accepted risk. The coordinator is trusted, so catalog hash authority is consistent with the model.

Open integration questions: (1) The consent scope now covers catalog builds the operator did not individually select, and `ProviderLoop+AutopilotDownload` is referenced in the ModelAutopilotSettings.swift doc comment (lines 3-7) but its source is not supplied. Its download integrity, transport, storage bounds and verification against the catalog hash need review. This is new attack surface (A-004, T-012, T-027). (2) The `autopilotModelSet`, `reconcileAutopilotPlacements` and `recordAutopilotPlacement` implementations and the full ProviderLoop+AutopilotControl changes were not visible, so how autopilotSetAllows gates serving admission is unverified. (3) The T-041 prefix-cache interaction with held or adopted models is unaffected in the visible code.
